# Search syntax

<!-- Generated by scripts/make_syntax_doc.py from the search engine's own table. -->

Type words to search card names, and add filters to narrow the results. The same page is
inside the app, under **Syntax**, with every example clickable. The filter panel on the
home page writes these queries for you.

## The basics

| You type | You get |
|---|---|
| `lightning bolt` | Cards whose name contains both words |
| `"serra angel"` | Quotes keep words together |
| `!"Lightning Bolt"` | An exclamation mark asks for the exact name |
| `t:dragon c:r` | Filters are written `key:value`, and all of them must match |
| `t:elf or t:goblin` | Either one or the other |
| `(t:elf or t:goblin) mv<=2` | Parentheses group, as in arithmetic |
| `c:r -t:creature` | A minus sign excludes |

Number filters accept `:` `=` `!=` `<` `<=` `>` `>=`, as in `mv<=3` or `pow>=5`.
Upper and lower case do not matter.

## Colours

Write any combination of `w` `u` `b` `r` `g`, a colour's name, `c` for colourless or `m`
for multicolour.

| You type | You get |
|---|---|
| `c:rg` | Cards that are at least red and green |
| `c=rg` | Exactly red and green |
| `c<=rg` | Red, green, both, or colourless |
| `c:c` | Colourless cards |
| `c:m` | Cards of two or more colours |
| `id:wub` | Cards that fit in a white-blue-black Commander deck |

## One result per card, or per printing

A search normally shows each card once, with the printing that matches best. Add
`unique:prints` to see every printing. Tokens and other extras are hidden unless you ask
for a set, a collector number, or add `include:extras`.

## All filters

| Filter | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | Card name contains (= for the exact name) | `name:bolt` |
| `o` `oracle` | Rules text contains | `o:"draw a card"` |
| `t` `type` | Type line contains | `t:legendary t:dragon` |
| `kw` `keyword` | Has a keyword ability | `kw:flying` |
| `c` `color` `colour` | Colours | `c:rg` `c=w` |
| `id` `identity` | Colour identity (fits in a deck of these colours) | `id:wub` |
| `mv` `cmc` | Mana value | `mv<=3` |
| `m` `mana` | Mana cost contains | `m:2rr` `m:{G}{G}` |
| `pow` `power` | Power | `pow>=5` |
| `tou` `toughness` | Toughness | `tou<2` |
| `loy` `loyalty` | Loyalty | `loy=3` |
| `r` `rarity` | Rarity | `r:mythic` `r>=rare` |
| `s` `e` `set` `edition` | Set code | `set:mh3` |
| `cn` `number` | Collector number | `cn:161` |
| `st` | Set type | `st:expansion` |
| `f` `format` `legal` | Legal in a format | `f:modern` |
| `a` `artist` | Artist name contains | `a:"rebecca guay"` |
| `ft` `flavor` | Flavour text contains | `ft:urza` |
| `year` | Year of the printing | `year>=2020` |
| `date` | Release date of the printing | `date>=2024-01-01` |
| `eur` | Price in euro | `eur<5` |
| `usd` | Price in US dollars | `usd>=20` |
| `is` | One of: foil, nonfoil, etched, reprint, promo, digital, extra, dfc | `is:foil` |
| `have` | I own any printing of this card (yes / no) | `have:yes` |
| `haveprint` | I own this exact printing (yes / no) | `set:arn haveprint:no` |
| `qty` | Copies I own of this printing | `qty>=4` |
| `loc` `location` | I keep it in a location named like | `loc:"blue box"` |
| `cond` | I own it in this condition | `cond:nm` |
| `finish` | I own it in this finish | `finish:foil` |
| `lang` | I own it in this language | `lang:it` |
| `deck` | In a deck whose name contains | `deck:"dragons"` |
| `unique` | Show cards (default) or every printing | `unique:prints` |
| `order` | Sort by: name, mv, released, rarity, price, set, type | `order:price` |
| `dir` | Sort direction: asc or desc | `dir:desc` |
| `include` | Also show tokens and other extras | `include:extras` |

## Your collection in a search

`have:` is about the card, whatever the printing; `haveprint:`, `qty`, `loc:`, `cond:`,
`finish:` and `lang:` are about the exact printing shown. So `set:mh3 haveprint:no
unique:prints` lists the printings of a set you are missing, and `have:yes t:dragon` every
dragon you own in any printing.

The switch beside the Search button writes `haveprint:yes` into the search for you, and
takes it out again: searching your collection is that one filter and nothing else.

## Limits

A search can be at most 2,000 characters and 100 terms long.
